tagline: A western border province with a huge waterfall deep in the jungle
introHtml:
Tak is a long province straddling two sides. The town side is quiet, sitting along the Ping River next to Bhumibol Dam, the largest dam in Thailand. The other side, across the hills, is Mae Sot, a border town next to Myanmar that buzzes with markets, trade, and Burmese food mixed with Shan flavors.

Most people who come to Tak are really heading to Umphang to see Thi Lo Su, a huge waterfall deep in the jungle that takes a drive through thousands of curves to reach. It suits people who love real nature, don't mind the long haul, and want to see a border town that isn't crowded yet.
bestTime: November–February, cool and green, good for hiking and waterfalls. Thi Lo Su has the most water in late rainy season into early winter.

highlights.name: Thi Lo Su Waterfall
highlights.blurb: A huge waterfall in the heart of Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary, a wide curtain of water falling over a limestone cliff. It's the main reason people come to Tak.

highlights.name: Mae Sot
highlights.blurb: A border town next to Myanmar with the Rim Moei market, Burmese temples, and Burmese-Shan food to eat and shop your way through.

highlights.name: Doi Hua Mot
highlights.blurb: A bare grassy ridge in Umphang that looks out over a valley full of morning fog. A popular viewpoint on the way to Thi Lo Su.

highlights.name: Bhumibol Dam
highlights.blurb: The largest curved concrete dam in Thailand, holding back the Ping River into a long reservoir. You can take a boat to see both banks.

highlights.name: Tak town by the Ping
highlights.blurb: A small, quiet town along the Ping River with the Somphot Krung Rattanakosin bridge, a walking street, and the old Trok Ban Chin Chinese quarter.

highlights.name: Highway 1090 to Umphang
highlights.blurb: A winding mountain road from Mae Sot into Umphang that people call the sky road, running through a thousand curves and valley views.

foodScene.name: Burmese and Shan food
foodScene.note: Mae Sot is a border town with Burmese khao soi, kaeng hang le, tea-leaf salad, and Burmese-style snacks at markets and shops around town.

foodScene.name: Sukhothai noodles and boat noodles
foodScene.note: Tak town eats sweet-leaning noodles much like Sukhothai's, found at shops in town and along the roadside.

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Nam phrik num, sai ua, and kaeng hang le are found all over the province, northern-style mixed with Burmese flavors near the border.

foodScene.name: Rim Moei market in Mae Sot
foodScene.note: A border market with Burmese snacks, dried goods, spices, and fruit at local prices to graze through.

foodScene.name: Tak walking street
foodScene.note: The riverside walking street in town has street food, local sweets, and snacks for an evening stroll.

foodScene.name: Miang Chom Phon
foodScene.note: A snack tied to Tak, leaves wrapped around miang filling with a punchy sauce. You can buy it to take home.

foodScene.name: Mu krata and casual evening spots
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with plenty of grill-your-own places to choose from in both Tak town and Mae Sot.

foodScene.name: Cafes in Mae Sot and town
foodScene.note: Small cafes have opened in Mae Sot and along the Ping, good for a coffee break after a long drive or walking around town.

attractions.name: Thi Lo Su Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A huge waterfall in Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary, a wide curtain of water over a limestone cliff. Reaching it takes a drive and a jungle walk.

attractions.name: Doi Hua Mot
attractions.blurb: A bare grassy ridge in Umphang with a valley full of morning fog. A good photo stop on the way to Thi Lo Su.

attractions.name: Bhumibol Dam
attractions.blurb: Thailand's largest curved dam holding back the Ping River, with a wide reservoir where you can take a boat and see the dam wall.

attractions.name: Mae Sot
attractions.blurb: A border town next to Myanmar with the Rim Moei market, Burmese temples, and border food for a full day of wandering.

attractions.name: Wat Thai Watthanaram
attractions.blurb: A Shan temple in Mae Sot with tiered Burmese-style roofs, a large reclining Buddha, and border-region art to see.

attractions.name: Umphang
attractions.blurb: A deep-jungle district at the end of Highway 1090, the base for Thi Lo Su, river rafting, and serious nature.

attractions.name: King Taksin Shrine and Trok Ban Chin
attractions.blurb: Tak town has the King Taksin shrine and the old Trok Ban Chin Chinese quarter along the Ping, with wooden houses and old shops to walk past.

attractions.name: Pha Charoen Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tiered limestone waterfall along the Mae Sot–Umphang road, a good stop for a swim along the way.
